trust_decision.summary: Before an OAuth2 authorization-endpoint error is turned into a 302, the requested redirect_uri must be resolved to a registered client and validated with client.check_redirect_uri (with the registered default URI used when the parameter is absent); the decision point for the unsupported_response_type error is AuthorizationServer.get_authorization_grant, which feeds OAuth2Error.__call__ -> add_params_to_uri -> Location header.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names 'open redirect via unsupported response_type'; the only construction of UnsupportedResponseTypeError in the tree is this raise, which passes the raw request.payload.redirect_uri into the error that becomes the Location header.

fix_sites.entry_point: AuthorizationServer.get_authorization_grant (public API; reached over HTTP by the /authorize route through get_consent_grant and create_authorization_response)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The OIDC core grants are a separate package implementing OpenID Connect flows; the failing request there raises invalid_scope for a missing 'openid' scope, not unsupported_response_type, so the advisory's named error and the fix in the OAuth2 authorization server appear not to apply.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A request with an existing client_id and a registered redirect_uri must still be answered with 302 + error=unsupported_response_type, and a request with an existing client_id and no redirect_uri must still redirect to client.get_default_redirect_uri(); only the unknown/unregistered cases become a 400 body. Pinned tests already pin both sides (test_invalid_response_type expects the redirect, test_authorization_none_grant expects the 400 body).

O6_input_shapes: client_id present but unknown to query_client -> no redirect
client_id valid + redirect_uri present and registered -> redirect to it
client_id valid + redirect_uri present but not registered -> no redirect
client_id valid + redirect_uri parameter omitted -> redirect to client.get_default_redirect_uri()
response_type present but unregistered, and response_type missing entirely (None)
parameters delivered in the query string (GET) or in the form body (POST), merged by the framework payload wrapper

O8_uncovered_routes.route: OpenID implicit authorize request whose scope lacks 'openid' raises InvalidScopeError with the raw request payload redirect_uri before the client is looked up or the redirect_uri validated, so the error becomes a 302 to an attacker URI
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: OIDC grant, different spec and a different error code (invalid_scope); looks like a scope-validation concern rather than the unsupported_response_type redirect the advisory names
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (authlib/oidc/core/grants) from the landing point in authlib/oauth2/rfc6749

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Same missing-openid-scope redirect in the OpenID hybrid grant (response_type 'code id_token' etc.), again with the raw payload redirect_uri used before client/redirect validation
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Hybrid flow is a separate grant class registered only on OIDC servers; the failure is a scope error, and the advisory's fix touched the shared authorization server, implying the grant layer was considered out of scope
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package and a second grant file next to the implicit one

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Second implementation of the redirect_uri check (e.g. in an integration client mixin) that re-derives the registered URI from storage instead of calling check_redirect_uri
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The base check is a static helper that grants call; every integration supplies its own Client class, so a maintainer could plausibly add a local 'resolve and validate redirect_uri' helper next to the model and use it only in the happy path

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An error raised while parsing/replacing the request-object payload before validation, carrying the JWT claim redirect_uri
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The extension installs a before_get_authorization_grant hook that swaps request.payload wholesale, so the redirect-issuing code reads claims that a different layer produced

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-protocol copy of 'error response = redirect to the callback' that skips a redirect_uri check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The OAuth 1 server already redirects to a callback stored at request-token time without checking it against the client, so copying that pattern into a second transport/version is natural

O9_family: CWE-601 URL redirection to untrusted site (open redirect) in an OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint error path

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools/pip install (cryptography dependency), pytest with tox envs (core/flask/django/clients/jose), uv/pytest-env
O10_build.project_tests: tests/flask/test_oauth2/ (test_authorization_code_grant.py, test_oauth2_server.py, test_openid_hybrid_grant.py, test_openid_implict_grant.py), tests/core/test_oauth2/, tests/django/test_oauth2/; sqlite in-memory, Flask/Django test clients, no network needed

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete the redirect_uri= argument from the UnsupportedResponseTypeError so this error never redirects — passes the added 'does not redirect' test but breaks the pinned test_invalid_response_type expectation that a registered client still receives error=unsupported_response_type.

out_of_scope_notes: OAuth 1.0 server stores the client-supplied oauth_callback unvalidated at the temporary-credential step and later redirects to it (authlib/oauth1/rfc5849/authorization_server.py:53-60,155-164) — a same-class open redirect in a different protocol, outside this advisory; noted only.
The fix commit also adds an unrelated test (test_missing_scope_empty_default) about get_allowed_scope returning an empty string; no matching source change is in the diff.
